Function declaration and check path are covered by hello and conformance seed.
Small native run behavior is covered by the checked Linux x86-64 lane.
Struct construction/field behavior is covered by a run conformance case.
Import behavior is covered for the active module resolver surface.
Positive effect subtyping behavior is checked.
Missing-effect diagnostic behavior is checked.
Borrow/release and conflict cases are checked; this is not a full Rust-equivalent ownership claim.
Constrained generic struct parsing/running is checked.
Constrained multi-parameter generic function behavior is checked.
Basic Knowledge values and uncertainty output are checked.
GUM compliance and ISO budget examples are checked.
Boundary diagnostics prevent silent unwrap and missing epistemic effect.
Units exist in fixtures, but broad user-facing claims need more conformance coverage.
Refinement support is a beta/prototype surface with a dedicated gate.
GPU support requires named hardware/gate evidence and is not a broad runtime claim.
Bounded stdlib support is checked through inventory and package-backed epistemic/GUM/units/formats/io/PBPK workflows; broad callability and hyper/science lanes remain separate claims.
Spec note and closure fixtures need reconciliation in the next spec-sync lane; treat closures as not user-safe for public claims until resolved.
Local package manifests, imports, package tool smoke, and local registry design are checked; no public registry launch is claimed.
Formatter, file-backed REPL, preview LSP, and VS Code/Helix/Neovim editor wiring are checked by a bounded support gate; pure-Sounio LSP rebuild and mature IDE surfaces remain out of scope.
